subject: Fast Onramp: MAP for POC network + auth handoff
messages:
From: Alec Turner <alec.turner@acmehealth.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@acmehealth.com>, Priya Malhotra <priya.malhotra@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff info (MAP)

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency numbers. We'd like to move fast on a short POC to validate inference costs and throughput in our staging region. To keep procurement and security happy, can you share a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that includes the specific items we need to complete on our side for environment setup (org provisioning, API keys, IP allowlist, VPC peering)?

High level timeline we want: 2-week sandbox evaluation, then a 2-week load test period. Ideal start: week of 3/6.

Questions right away:
- Can Redwood provide ephemeral test API keys scoped to a single staging org?
- What exact CIDR block(s) do you need for peering, and do you support Cloud Router / dynamic routes or only static?
- Who on your side will create the MAP and own signoffs?

If you can drop a MAP draft and the minimal checklist (API key request, service account names, allowlist CSV template), we can get this into our SRE queue.

Appreciate it — Alec
Alec Turner
Head of Platform Engineering, ACME Health

From: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: Alec Turner <alec.turner@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-01T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: POC kickoff info (MAP)

Hi Alec — great to hear you want to move quickly. I've attached a one-page MAP and a small seedlist CSV for your SRE team to fill out. Summary answers to your questions below, plus an initial close timeline aligned to your 2+2 plan.

Quick answers:
- Ephemeral test keys: yes — we can issue time-limited tokens scoped to a single staging org and a single model. We'll provide both long-lived service account creds (for peering and infra) and ephemeral test keys for app-level traffic.
- Peering: we support both static route VPC peering and cloud-router BGP sessions in GCP/Azure; for AWS we do VPC peering + route table entries. For the POC we recommend a single /28 for test peering to avoid complicated ACL changes. If you need, we can accept a /27 as well.
- MAP owner: I'll own the MAP and milestone signoffs from Redwood. Marissa will run the network coordination, and Soojin will handle the credentials and security questionnaire items.

Proposed MAP milestones (brief):
1) Day 0-2: MAP sign + account seeds (your SRE provides org name, primary contact, and allowlist CSV)
2) Day 3-5: Network setup — exchange peering details, confirm routing, and open the peering request
3) Day 6-8: Credentials — Redwood issues service-account long-lived creds for infra + ephemeral API tokens for app testing
4) Day 9-14: Sandbox validation — basic traffic, functional checks, and initial cost sampling
5) Week 3-4: Load test window — full throughput runs, monitoring, and cost/latency report

Attachments in this thread: ACME_MAP_v1.pdf (one-pager MAP) and acme_network_seedlist.csv (CSV template for allowlist/peering).

Next steps: can your SRE fill the CSV and confirm a preferred start date (3/6 or 3/13)? I'll schedule the internal ops tasks once we have the CSV.

Thanks,
Maya Srinivasan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
M: +1 415 555 0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-02T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Fast Onramp MAP — network items (internal)

Maya — forwarding ACME's CSV templates and Alec's note. Marissa here (ops/network). Quick internal checklist for our side so we can be ready when ACME returns the filled seedlist:

Action items for Redwood infra team (assign ASAP):
- Reserve ephemeral peering CIDR (/28) in us-west-2 and validate against current peering roster.
- Prepare VPC peering playbook for AWS (include instructions for route table updates and security group entries).
- Generate two artifacts to send back with the MAP: 1) service-account provisioning manifest (names/roles) and 2) ephemeral token issuance steps.
- Smoke test an ephemeral token against staging endpoint: https://staging-api.redwood.ai/v1/echo (token scope: model:readonly).

Attachments to include in external reply: map_v1.pdf (signed copy), network_seedlist_filled.csv (when they return it), and a one-page 'peering runbook' PDF.

Soojin — can you pre-create the service-account templates and the ephemeral-token TTL options (1h, 8h, 7d) so we can offer choices? I'll start the CIDR reservation and draft the peering work order.

-Marissa
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Malhotra <priya.malhotra@acmehealth.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alec Turner <alec.turner@acmehealth.com>, DevOps Team <devops@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2028-03-03T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fast Onramp: MAP for POC network + auth handoff

Thanks Maya — the MAP and templates look good. We've filled the seedlist and attached acme_network_seedlist_filled.csv. Quick confirmations from our side:

- Preferred start: week of 3/13 (SRE backlog that week clears).
- We accept the /28 test peering; we've assigned 10.11.12.0/28 for the peering CIDR and will open the VPC peering request once you confirm your target VPC ID and account number.
- Ephemeral token TTL: we'll take 8h for initial testing, with ability to request 1h for smaller teams.

Next ask: can you provide the specific service-account names and a DocuSign link for the MAP sign-off? We need an internal approvals packet to move this to procurement.

Attached: acme_network_seedlist_filled.csv (text/csv)

Looking forward — Priya
Priya Malhotra
SRE Manager, ACME Health
